text:
Brayden Point is back from injured reserve and looking like himself, even if the goals haven't caught up yet. Tampa activated him on November 18 (the same move put Conor Geekie on IR), and he has three assists in four games since.

The process is strong. Point is generating 1.25 expected goals per 60 minutes on his own shots, the best rate of his last two seasons, and the Lightning get about 60% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. His skating numbers are elite: 108 bursts over 20 mph on NHL EDGE, 99th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on two-thirds of his entries last season.

What's missing is finish. He has five goals on 8.3 expected, shooting 10.9% against a likely range around 13%. That is the opposite of last season, when Evolving-Hockey noted his results ran well ahead of his chances. The truth is probably somewhere in the middle, and over 21 games we'd lean on the chances: 18 points so far, with more goals likely to follow the looks he keeps getting.
